title: Containerfile for a Python script or job
when: The user wants to run a Python script, nightly job or small worker inside a container with pinned dependencies, unbuffered logs and no root user.
prompt:
Goal: A Containerfile that builds a virtual environment from pinned requirements and runs one Python module as an unprivileged user.
Steps:
1. Stage deps: FROM python:3.12.7-slim AS deps; RUN python -m venv /opt/venv; ENV PATH="/opt/venv/bin:$PATH".
2. COPY requirements.txt alone, then RUN pip install --no-cache-dir -r requirements.txt; every line pins with ==, plus --require-hashes when hashes exist.
3. Compile wheels only in this stage.
4. Stage run: FROM python:3.12.7-slim; COPY --from=deps /opt/venv /opt/venv; ENV PATH="/opt/venv/bin:$PATH" PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1 PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1.
5. RUN useradd --system --uid 10001 --no-create-home app; COPY --chown=app:app src/ /app/; WORKDIR /app; USER app.
6. ENTRYPOINT ["python", "-m", "job"] so run time arguments reach argparse; defaults go in CMD.
7. Outputs go under /data (VOLUME /data), never /app; failures return a non zero exit code.
Quality bar:
- Log lines reach the container log at once.
- Two builds from the same files install the same versions.
- One container runs one job and exits.
Pitfalls:
- Unpinned pip installs, so a rebuild pulls a breaking release.
- Compilers left in the final image.
- Root user leaving files on the mount the host user cannot delete.
- Shell form ENTRYPOINT that drops the arguments.
Verify:
- [ ] FROM tags name exact Python versions.
- [ ] USER app comes before ENTRYPOINT.
- [ ] requirements.txt pins every package.
- [ ] Outputs go to the volume.
Output: Containerfile, requirements.txt and a run example in README.md.

examples.input: run my python report script in a container every night
examples.output: Containerfile on python:3.12.7-slim with a venv stage, useradd app, ENTRYPOINT ["python", "-m", "report"], /data volume
